message.reasoning:
We need to determine failure mode: collisions dominate (9 of 10 runs fail due to collision). Need to analyze why code fails: it doesn't use sensors, so moving objects not detected, leading to collisions early. Evidence: first_not_on_map shows detection times but controller ignores. Also stop_turn_episodes show many stop-turns (maybe due to waypoint following). Collisions happen at early times when object appears within 2m (first_not_on_map within 2m at ~1s) but robot still moving at ~1.5 m/s, not stopping. So failure mode: collision due to lack of dynamic obstacle avoidance. Need to propose adding sensor-based detection and reactive stopping/avoidance. Target: modify controller to incorporate lidar2d_points detection of non-map points (first_not_on_map) and if any within safety distance (e.g., 1.5 m) then stop and wait until cleared or perform simple avoidance (e.g., turn away). Could also add simple reactive behavior: if moving object detected within 1.5 m in front sector, set v=0, w=0.5 rad/s to turn away, maybe resume after cleared.

Provide evidence: e.g., run c2t0_s1554098519 collision at 3.33s, first_not_on_map within 2m at 1.05s, robot still moving 1.5 m/s at collision. Another run c2t0_s1302393766 collision at 29.38s, first_not_on_map within 2m at 27.85s, robot still moving 1.09 m/s. So pattern.

Thus failure mode = collision.

Target: controller (add sensor detection). Direction: add code to read front lidar, filter points not belonging to map (use provided first_not_on_map logic? but we can approximate by checking points that are not within any static obstacle bounding boxes). Simpler: use lidar2d_points('front') and detect any point within 1.2 m ahead (bearing +-30°). If found, set v=0 and rotate slowly until clear. Also keep waypoint logic but pause.

Will propose adding a new helper function _is_moving_obstacle_near() using lidar2d_points and static map boxes.

But cannot import map data? We have WALLS, FIXED_OBSTACLES, MISSION boxes. Could compute distances to those to filter static. Simpler: use first_not_on_map detection via lidar2d_points and compare to map? Hard. Could just treat any point within 1.2 m as obstacle (including static) but static already avoided by waypoints, so fine.

Thus modify controller to check front lidar each call, if any point distance < safety_dist and bearing within +/-30°, then stop and turn away (e.g., w = 0.5). After clearance, resume.
